clue.text: Disgusted, being fond of brew that's spoiled

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined or messed up, so the preceding words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loves their brew but finds this batch has gone off, and is put out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's spoiled' rearranges FOND OF BREW; 'being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Browned off is British slang for fed up or annoyed, close to revolted or sickened.

clue.text: Wrongly blamed for uproar

indicators.note: done wrongly means done incorrectly, so the letters of the next word are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone unfairly accused causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after an old London asylum, is a scene of chaos and noise.

clue.text: Object to work on model

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a job involving a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' reads as a noun but works as the verb, to sit for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To object to something is to resist or stand against it.

clue.text: Science gives straight-forward account of the past

parts.note: natural behaviour is plain and unaffected
a history is a record of past events

explanation.surface: A scientific discipline delivers a plain chronicle of bygone times.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural history is the study of plants and animals, a branch of biology.

clue.text: Making a claim is very hard

explanation.surface: Insisting on one's rights is tough going.
explanation.definitionFit: Demanding means insisting on something as one's due, and also describes a strenuous, testing task.

clue.text: Last piece of fish, a pound

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish
L stands for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: The remaining portion of fish costs a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Final means coming at the end, the closing one.

clue.text: Heather dropping a boy

indicators.note: dropping a letter means leaving it out of the word for heather

parts.note: erica is the botanical genus name for heather

explanation.surface: A girl called Heather lets a boy fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a girl's name, but it is the plant, ERICA; 'dropping a' removes the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric is a male first name, and crosswords use boy for any male name.

clue.text: Evoking love, partly from anticipation

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Looking forward to something can stir feelings of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' points to a run of letters inside 'from anticipation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something romantic stirs feelings of passion or tenderness.

clue.text: Join Conservative on border

parts.note: CON is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British party
a verge is an edge or grassy roadside border

explanation.surface: An invitation to sign up with the Tories at the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join' looks like an order to enlist with the party, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To converge is to come together and meet at one point.

clue.text: Small gift one may make to filing clerks

indicators.note: the words that follow are raw material from which something new may be made by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A little present someone might give the office filing staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may make' rearranges TO FILING CLERKS; 'one' is a link. A stocking filler is a small Christmas present put in a stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocking filler is an inexpensive present tucked into a Christmas stocking.

clue.text: Drank hard on return from this regimental HQ

indicators.note: on return means the word for drank hard is read the other way round

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol heavily

explanation.surface: Soldiers who drink heavily coming back from their base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' turns TOPED backwards; 'from this' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is the headquarters or base of a regiment where recruits are trained.

clue.text: Small fellow needed for missile

parts.note: minute means tiny
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A short chap is required for a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuteman is the name of an American intercontinental ballistic missile.

clue.text: He doesn't get a place in the race

definitions.text: He doesn't get a place in the race

parts.words: He doesn't get a place in the race
parts.note: describes a runner who finishes outside the first few positions in a horse race

explanation.surface: A runner fails to finish in the top positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' is the racing sense, finishing in the first two or three.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a competitor who finishes unplaced, and by extension any loser.

clue.text: Permit debauchery

explanation.surface: Permission to indulge in wild living.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is an official permit, and licence also means excessive freedom or licentious behaviour.

clue.text: Simple task, piloting a prairie schooner?

explanation.surface: Steering a covered wagon across flat grasslands is an easy job.
explanation.walkthrough: A prairie schooner is a covered wagon of the American West, which 'sails' across the plains.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain sailing is an easy undertaking, and literally voyaging over the plains as a wagon would.

clue.text: It's something for referee to abandon observation

parts.note: to stop doing something is to abandon it
a watch is a period of observation or guard

explanation.surface: A referee must give up watching closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopwatch is a timer used by an official to time a match.

clue.text: Confess capturing pawn was very bad

indicators.note: capturing means holding another piece inside, as one chess piece takes another

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
to hock something is to pawn it

explanation.surface: A chess player admits that taking a pawn was a dreadful move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pawn' is not the chess piece but the verb, to hock; 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocking is used informally to mean dreadful or appalling.

clue.text: Special Constable criticised and discarded

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for Special Constable, a volunteer police officer in Britain
rapped means reprimanded or criticised sharply

explanation.surface: A volunteer policeman is reprimanded and dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapped means thrown away or abandoned as useless.

clue.text: Spasmodic trouble for computer pirate?

explanation.surface: A computer hacker suffers fits of bother.
explanation.walkthrough: A hacking cough is a dry, harsh repeated cough; the second reading is a pun on hacking as breaking into computers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacking cough comes in harsh fits, and the phrase also suggests an illness suited to an online intruder.

clue.text: Walk, say, the Russian plain

indicators.note: say tells us the word for walk is spoken, giving a word that sounds identical

parts.note: a step is a single pace of walking

explanation.surface: A stroll, perhaps, across the plains of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The steppe is the vast treeless grassland of Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Secluded spot for adjournment

explanation.surface: A quiet place to go during a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a hidden nook or alcove, and also a break in proceedings of parliament or a court.

clue.text: After talk, let's return property

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the first in the answer

parts.note: a chat is a talk

indicators.note: return says the word let is written backwards

parts.note: the word let, its 's read as is

explanation.surface: Following a discussion, a landlord gives back possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is an item of movable personal possession.

clue.text: Student beat a pack-animal

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
to lam is to thrash or hit

explanation.surface: A pupil whips an animal used for carrying loads.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a South American beast of burden used to carry loads.

clue.text: Penny used to buy this pipe

definitions.text: Penny used to buy this pipe

parts.words: Penny used to buy this pipe
parts.note: names a cheap tin musical instrument once priced at a single copper coin

explanation.surface: Once a penny would purchase this musical pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The penny whistle, or tin whistle, is a simple cheap pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle is a small simple wind instrument, a pipe that is blown.

clue.text: Vital to bring in a set of books

parts.note: to import is to bring goods in from abroad
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: It is essential to bring in a collection of volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Important means of great significance, essential.

clue.text: Left part of church to fall into disuse

parts.note: an apse is the vaulted recess at the east end of a church

explanation.surface: An abandoned section of a church has gone to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: To lapse is to cease being in use or force, as a custom or policy does.

clue.text: Gallery of immortals

explanation.surface: A gallery displaying the deathless ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The gods' is the highest gallery in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The gods is slang for a theatre's top gallery, and deities are the immortal beings of myth.

clue.text: Single-parent child, but left shares in profusion

definitions.note: the clue names a person; the answer is the adjective describing such a child

indicators.note: in profusion suggests things scattered lavishly about, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A lone parent's offspring, yet abandoned shares are plentiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in profusion' rearranges LEFT SHARES; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A child raised by a mother alone has no dad present.
